1. (Currently Amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a hardware entropy source including at least one ring oscillator;
one or more logic circuits physically coupled to the hardware entropy source and configured to receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from the hardware entropy source;
one or more logic circuits physically configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;
one or more logic circuits physically configured to seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
one or more logic circuits physically configured to generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
one or more logic circuits physically configured to produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number, wherein the system implements countermeasures to phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator based entropy source.

2. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number, and wherein the countermeasures include at least one of: jittering the ring oscillator, introducing random delays, or applying feedback mechanisms to prevent phase synchronization.

3. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source includes at least one ring oscillator, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the at least one ring oscillator.

5. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source is a single hardware entropy source, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware entropy source.

6. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source comprises a plurality of independent hardware entropy sources, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware entropy sources.

7. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

8. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 7, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

9. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

10. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

11. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

12. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.

13. (Currently Amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware entropy source including at least one ring oscillator;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value;
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number; and
implementing countermeasures to phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator based entropy source.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number, and wherein the countermeasures include at least one of: jittering the ring oscillator, introducing random delays, or applying feedback mechanisms to prevent phase synchronization.

15. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least: implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware entropy source includes at least one ring oscillator, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the at least one ring oscillator.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware entropy source is a single hardware entropy source, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware entropy source.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware entropy source comprises a plurality of independent hardware entropy sources, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware entropy sources.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

21. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a hash function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

24. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
